title: Cap. X Arg. VI close: unbelief foreseen in negation of efficacious grace; Augustine De praedest. sanct. 6 — preparing / not preparing the will precedes foresight of faith or unbelief
pass_a_gloss: Therefore reprobation is not to be placed from foresight of antecedent unbelief, nor election from foresight of faith; but the final unbelief of the reprobate is foreseen in the antecedent negation of efficacious grace, and the persevering faith of the elect is foreseen in the antecedent preparation of efficacious grace: so that on both sides principate, authority, superiority, and determinative power, whether of things future or not-future, may be with God as supreme arbiter. This is that which Augustine taught, de praedest. sanct. cap. 6. Some believe, others contradict. These therefore will to believe; but those will not. Who is ignorant of this? who denies this? But since unto some the will is prepared by the Lord, unto others it is not prepared, &c. Whence it is plain that the decree concerning human wills to be prepared and not to be prepared is prior to foresight either of human faith or of unbelief: Which is just as if we should say that the predestination and preterition of singular persons is prior to absolute foreknowledge of faith or unbelief in the same.
pass_b_english: So reprobation is not to be set from foresight of antecedent unbelief, nor election from foresight of faith. Final unbelief in the reprobate is foreseen in the antecedent denial of efficacious grace; persevering faith in the elect is foreseen in the antecedent preparation of that grace—so that on both sides principate, authority, superiority, and determining power over futures and non-futures rest with God as supreme arbiter. That is what Augustine taught (De praedestinatione sanctorum 6): Some believe; others contradict. These will to believe; those will not. Who does not know this? Who denies it? But since the Lord prepares the will for some and not for others, and so on. So the decree to prepare or not prepare human wills is prior to foresight of human faith or unbelief—which is as much as to say that predestination and preterition of singular persons is prior to absolute foreknowledge of faith or unbelief in them.
source_text: Non ergo reprobatio ponenda est ex praevisione antecedaneae infidelitatis, nec electio ex praevisione fidei; sed infidelitas reprobatorum finalis praevidetur in antecedente negatione gratiae efficacis, et fides electorum perseverans praevidetur in antecedente praeparatione gratiae efficacis: ut utrobique principatus, authoritas, superioritas et determinativa potestas sive rerum futurarum sive non-futurarum sit penes Deum tanquam supremum arbitrum. Hoc illud est quod docuit Augustinus, de praedest. sanct. cap. 6. Alii credunt, alii contradictunt. Volunt ergo isti credere; nolunt autem illi. Quis hoc ignoret? quis hoc neget? Sed cum aliis praeparetur, aliis non praeparetur voluntas a Domino, &c. Unde patet decretum de praeparandis et non praeparandis humanis voluntatibus esse praevisa sive fide sive infidelitate humana prius: Quod perinde est ac si diceremus, praedestinationem et praeteritionem singularium personarum esse absoluta praescientia fidei aut infidelitatis in eisdem priorem.
